pass_a_gloss: Logos 3. [Lemma, Isaiah 45:18-19:] Thus says the Lord, the one who made the heaven, this one who showed forth the earth and made it, this one marked it out. Not for empty did he make it, but to be inhabited. I am the Lord, and there is not yet [another]. Not in secret have I spoken, nor in a dark place of earth. I did not say to the seed of Jacob: Seek vain. I am the Lord speaking righteousness and announcing truth. Having proclaimed beforehand the arrival of the Saviour of us all, Christ, and having marked out the time of the salvation, at which all, having let go the darkness of the ancient ignorance, will move over to the light of the true knowledge of God, he makes in these a necessary exhortation to Jews and Greeks, adding clear the things through which they will know very plainly both that he himself is God of all and creator, and that there is no other beside him. For this reason he says: Thus says the Lord, and not simply Lord, for there are very many both in heaven and on the earth who have received the name as in loose use; but that one himself who by nature and truly is this which he is also said to be, and as from the things achieved having the glory not falsified. For this, he says, is the Lord who made the heaven; an all-great thing toward proof of the highest renown, and of all-powerful pre-eminence, is to have made the heaven and shown forth the earth, and to have founded it. For he himself marked it out, that is, being hidden in deeps, invisible and unconstructed of old, he showed it visible and worked. For he marked it out; for he said, according to the faith of the books of Moses: Let the water be gathered into one gathering, and let the dry appear. So it appeared from waters, and being under water and wholly unworked he set it apart in part, putting bars and gates on the deeps, and separating it very well from the waters. And that he brought it forth usefully for this and necessarily, not so that it be seen only, but so that it have the inhabitants, clearly those formed from it, just as indeed also heaven the holy angels, he made clear beforehand, saying: Not for empty did he make it, but to be inhabited. So a support and as some house it was shown to those treading it, that is, to us. And if we were brought forth by him toward existence, how is it not true to say that surely also for this we came to be, so that we might worship him and alone, and acknowledge him being generator of all [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Logos 3. “Thus says the Lord who made the heaven; He it is who showed forth the earth and made it; He it is who marked it out. He did not make it for nothing, but to be inhabited. I am the Lord, and there is no other. I have not spoken in secret, nor in a dark place of the earth. I did not say to the offspring of Jacob, ‘Seek what is vain.’ I am the Lord, who speaks righteousness and declares truth” (Isaiah 45:18-19).

Having proclaimed beforehand the coming of Christ, the Savior of us all, and having marked out the time of salvation, when all will leave the darkness of their old ignorance and pass over to the light of the true knowledge of God, he here gives a needful exhortation to Jews and Greeks alike. He adds clear proofs by which they will know very plainly that He is the God and Maker of all, and that there is no other besides Him.

That is why he says, “Thus says the Lord”; and not simply “Lord,” for there are very many in heaven and on earth who have received that name by a loose use of it (compare 1 Corinthians 8:5), but He Himself who by nature and in truth is what He is also called, and who, from the very things He has accomplished, has a glory that is not false. For this, he says, is the Lord who made the heaven. To have made the heaven, and to have shown forth the earth and set it firm, is a very great proof of supreme glory and almighty pre-eminence.

For He marked it out; that is, when of old it lay hidden in the deeps, invisible and unformed (Genesis 1:2), He made it visible and finished. He marked it out, for, as the books of Moses attest, He said: “Let the water be gathered into one gathering, and let the dry land appear” (Genesis 1:9). So it appeared out of the waters; and though it was under water and wholly unworked, He set it apart by itself, placing bars and gates on the deeps (compare Job 38:10) and separating it thoroughly from the waters.

That He brought it forth usefully and of necessity to this end, not only so that it might be seen but so that it might have inhabitants, namely those formed from it, just as heaven has the holy angels, he made clear beforehand by saying, “He did not make it for nothing, but to be inhabited.” So it was shown to be a support and, as it were, a house for those who tread on it, that is, for us. And if we were brought into existence by Him, how is it not true to say that we were surely made for this very reason, that we might worship Him and Him alone, and acknowledge Him who is the Author of all things …

choices.english: received that name by a loose use of it
choices.why: κατάχρησις, an improper or extended use of a word; others are called 'lord' only loosely.
Cyril explains it as God bringing the hidden earth into view (Genesis 1:9).
ὄχημα, that which carries; the earth bears those who tread it.
Before the waters were gathered, the earth was idle and unfinished.

choices.english: as the books of Moses attest
choices.why: πίστις here is the evidence of the books.
rejected: according to the faith of Moses
